name: SLAPJACK
description: Slapjack (or 'Slaps') is a children's card game that tests speed and reflexes. Players take turns flipping cards onto a central pile. When a Jack appears, the first player to slap the pile wins all the cards in the center. The goal is to collect the entire deck.

content.text: Slapjack (or 'Slaps') is a children's card game that tests speed and reflexes. Players take turns flipping cards onto a central pile. When a Jack appears, the first player to slap the pile wins all the cards in the center. The goal is to collect the entire deck.
Dates back to the 19th century as 'Beggar My Neighbor' variant. The physical act of slapping makes it a perennial favorite for kids.
Two to eight players; sources recommend about 4–10 for best play. Each player holds their cards as a face-down pile and takes turns flipping to a center pile. Play proceeds clockwise.
One standard 52-card French deck. The pack is divided roughly equally between all players; everyone holds their cards as a face-down pile. No jokers or extra cards are used.
Deal entirely to players face-down into personal piles.

items.text: Time limit: Set a time limit; the player with the most cards when time runs out wins.
Double Slap: Slap on matching doubles (e.g. 6-6) as well as on Jacks.
Say Slapjack: Player must say 'Slapjack!' when covering the pile; if they fail, they do not get the pile. If they say it and the card is not a Jack, the other players divide the pile.
